Distribution. China (Taiwan). Notes. Helcon albus Chou et Hsu from Taiwan is included in Wroughtonia, because it has a wide obtuse ventral protuberance on the hind femur, the hind tarsus is pale and the antenna has a white band. The species is included provisionally in the key on basis of the original description, because the holotype (and only known specimen of W. alba) was not available for examination. Spasskia anastasiae Belokobylskij from Far East Russia is included in Wroughtonia (as other Spasskia spp.) but is not close to the other species because of the obtuse ventral protuberance of the hind femur and the shape of the first tergite and of the occipital carina. In the key it will come near W. alba because the hind coxa are densely sculptured (transversely rugulose to rugose) dorsally; differs from W. alba by the complete dark brown or black antenna (with white band in W. alba), palpi dark brown basally (brownish yellow), temple and vertex densely and coarsely punctate-rugose (smooth) and hind coxa dark brown or black (brownish yellow).

d.a: Distribution: — Vietnam: Kon Tum Province (Pa Sy Waterfall ecotourism area in Kon Plong District). Conservation status: — Aspidistra mirostigma var. haui was observed in a single locality, and we estimate the only discovered population to include less than 250 mature individuals with the extent of occurrence (EOO) and area of occupancy (AOO) surely much less than 10 km 2. The area near the Pa Sy Waterfall inhabited by this variety is a tourist resort, and its aboriginal vegetation is almost completely destroyed. This area is currently not under any legal protection. Due to the fast decline of habitat quality, we assume that the variety stands at the verge of extinction in the wild. We therefore preliminarily assess its conservation status as Critically Endangered (CR B 1 ab (iii) + 2 ab (iii); C 1 a (i, ii) + b (i, ii )) following the formal criteria of IUCN (2025). Notes: — Aspidistra mirostigma var. haui differs from the type variety of A. mirostigma Tillich & Škorničk. in Leong-Škorničková et al. (2014: 34) in absence of keels on inner surface of perianth tube (vs. perianth tube inside with ca. 24 distinct keels), perianth lobes with 2 indistinct central ribs (vs. 2 prominent keels) between the lateral keels, stamens inserted at middle (vs. near the base) of the perianth tube, stigma apically flat, with 6 radially oriented pits on upper surface (vs. with apical part having the shape of a truncated cone and bearing numerous longitudinal grooves) and with 12 (vs. 6) dents along margin. Together with the finding described here as a separate variety, A. mirostigma is still considered endemic to Kon Plong District. Aspidistra mirostigma var. mirostigma has only been reported from its type locality, which is located 18 km from the population of A. mirostigma var. haui. Remarkably, the third currently available series of collections of A. mirostigma, the one obtained by B. Wynn-Jones at the type locality of the species (at least the specimen Wynn-Jones, BWJ 15796; photos LE: LE 01087125 https: // en. herbariumle. ru /? t = occ & id = 18649), demonstrates intermediate morphology, i. e. perianth tube with keels inside, 4 - keeled tepal lobes and stamens inserted near the base of the perianth tube as in A. mirostigma var. mirostigma, stigma with 12 dents at margin as in A. mirostigma var. haui, and low elevation at stigma apex being equally different from both varieties. The distribution pattern together with the morphological variation suggests that the two varieties are not strictly delimited from each other, and rather represent extreme variants of the gradual intraspecific diversity.
